design.alone_auc_population: FIT+MINE (MONITOR never read for a design decision)
design.stratum_rule: terciles of |alone-AUC - .5| over the 40 Track-B channels
design.mirrors: m3_concepts.py (A-side), K=8/3+3+2 there vs K=6/2+2+2 here

channels.name: Non-idiomatic English and grammatical slips
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract departs from fluent idiomatic English — agreement errors, article misuse, awkward collocations, malformed constructions. Score surface fluency only, not the clarity of the underlying ideas.

channels.name: A public repository URL appears in the abstract
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the abstract contains a real, public code or data link — a repository URL or hosted project address. Score 0 when there is no link. This is about a live public link, not about anonymised submission placeholders or promises to release later.

channels.name: Passive-voice density
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the abstract is written in the passive voice ('it is shown that', 'experiments were conducted', 'the model is trained') rather than the active voice. Score the grammatical construction only.

channels.name: Syntactic complexity independent of total length
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how long and multi-clausal the abstract's individual SENTENCES are — subordinate clauses, parentheticals, chains of qualifiers — judged independently of how long the abstract is overall. A short abstract of tangled sentences scores high; a long abstract of short sentences scores low.

channels.name: Abstract length and verbosity
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how long and densely packed the abstract is compared with a typical conference abstract: 0 for a very short abstract of a few sentences, 10 for one that runs long with many clauses and sub-points. Judge extent only; do not judge whether the length is warranted.

channels.name: Topic sits in a currently dominant research area
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how central the abstract's subject is to the areas that currently dominate machine-learning publishing — large language models, multimodal or vision-language models, diffusion and other generative models, agents. Score topic membership only; a careful paper on an unfashionable topic should score low here.

channels.name: Efficiency-vocabulary density
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how heavily the abstract uses efficiency register — efficient, lightweight, scalable, fast, low-cost, cheap, practical, resource-friendly. Count the vocabulary only, not whether efficiency was actually achieved or measured.

channels.name: Parenthetical example density
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how often the abstract inserts parenthetical examples or clarifications — '(e.g., ...)', '(such as ...)', '(i.e., ...)'. Count the parenthetical habit only.

channels.name: Poses a specific question and states its answer plainly
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract frames a specific answerable question and then gives the answer in plain terms, rather than describing an area of activity and a contribution to it. Score the question-and-answer structure, not the importance of the question.

channels.name: Belief-change — the output is a changed understanding rather than a delivered artifact
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the main thing a reader takes away is a revised belief about how something works, as opposed to a tool, model, or dataset they can now use. Both are legitimate contributions; score only which one the abstract is offering.

channels.name: Opens with a broad field-level platitude
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract's opening sentence is a generic statement about the field's importance or recent progress ('X has been widely used', 'X has made significant progress in recent years') rather than a statement specific to this work's problem. Score the opening move only.

channels.name: First-person narrative density
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how heavily the abstract is written in the first person plural — 'we propose', 'we show', 'we find', 'our method' — as opposed to impersonal or passive construction. Count the register only.

channels.name: Membership in the learning-theory / optimization subfield
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the abstract belongs to the learning-theory, optimization, or statistical-guarantees cluster — convergence rates, regret bounds, complexity results, estimator analysis. Score topic membership only; work of any quality in any other subfield scores 0.

channels.name: Self-referential discourse markers
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how often the abstract refers to itself as a document — 'In this paper', 'In this work', 'Here we', 'This paper proposes'. Count the self-reference only.

channels.name: Branded method name or acronym
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how strongly the work brands itself with a coined capitalised name or acronym for its method, system, dataset, or benchmark, and repeats that name through the abstract. Score the branding practice only.

channels.name: Signals of industrial-scale compute or frontier proprietary models
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract signals access to large-scale industrial resources: named proprietary frontier models used or compared against, explicit GPU counts or cluster scale, model sizes in billions of parameters, corpora at hundreds of millions of items. Score the resource signal only.

channels.name: Magnitude of the engineering or data resource the work required
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much construction effort the abstract evidences — corpora built, systems trained at multiple scales, pipelines assembled, annotations collected — judged from what is described as having been made, not from claims about importance.

channels.name: Raw LaTeX or markup residue left in the abstract
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much unrendered markup survives in the abstract text: LaTeX commands, math delimiters left as literal characters, escaped percent or backslash characters, footnote markers, markdown emphasis. Score the residue only, not the content it decorates.

channels.name: Membership in the privacy / security / adversarial-robustness subfield
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the abstract belongs to the privacy, security, adversarial-robustness, or attack-and-defence cluster of machine learning. Score topic membership only; work of any quality in any other subfield scores 0.

channels.name: Anonymized-repository or release-on-acceptance code boilerplate
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how prominently the abstract carries submission-time artifact boilerplate: an anonymised repository link (for example an anonymous code-hosting URL or a placeholder), or a promise that code or data will be released later or upon publication. Score 0 when no such statement appears; score by presence and prominence of the boilerplate, not by whether sharing is a good practice.

channels.name: Mathematical notation density in the abstract
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much formal mathematical notation appears in the abstract — inline symbols, variables, set or norm notation, complexity expressions, formulas. Score notational density only, not whether the mathematics is correct or deep.

channels.name: Discourse-connective scaffolding density
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how heavily the abstract uses sentence-initial connectives to scaffold its argument — However, Moreover, Furthermore, Thus, Therefore, In contrast, Specifically. Score the connective density only.

channels.name: Explicit priority or first-ness claims
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how prominently the abstract asserts priority — 'to the best of our knowledge, the first', 'for the first time', 'we present the first study of'. Score the assertion of priority only, not whether it is true or whether the work is novel.

channels.name: Applied-domain framing outside core machine learning
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the abstract is framed around an application domain outside core machine learning — medicine and clinical imaging, neuroscience and brain-computer interfaces, ecology and environment, field robotics, materials. Score domain framing only; core-ML work scores 0 regardless of quality.

channels.name: Density of promotional superlatives and hype vocabulary
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how heavily the abstract uses promotional vocabulary — remarkable, impressive, striking, significant, substantial, superior, novel, state-of-the-art, comprehensive, extensive. Count the promotional register, not whether the claims are true.

channels.name: Density of percentage figures
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many percentage figures the abstract reports. Count percentage-formatted numbers only; do not judge whether they are impressive or well-supported.

channels.name: Typographic emphasis used inside the abstract
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract uses typographic emphasis to direct attention — bold, italics, or emphasis markup around names, numbers, or claims. Score the emphasis practice only, regardless of what is emphasised.

channels.name: Self-description as novel or new
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how often the abstract describes its own contribution with the words novel, new, or first-of-its-kind. Count the lexical self-description only; do not judge whether the work is actually novel.

channels.name: "Framework" as the contribution noun
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract labels its own contribution a framework, paradigm, pipeline, or scheme rather than naming a concrete object such as an algorithm, model, dataset, bound, or result. Score the choice of noun only.

channels.name: Multiplicative speedup notation
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many multiplicative performance figures the abstract states — '3.04x', '91 times', '5 to 10 times faster', 'orders of magnitude'. Count the notation only; do not judge whether the speedup is real, fairly measured, or worth its cost.

channels.name: Membership in the graph-learning / GNN subfield
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the abstract belongs to the graph neural network, graph representation, or graph algorithms cluster. Score topic membership only; work of any quality in any other subfield scores 0.

channels.name: Enumeration of specific named models in a model zoo
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many specific named model checkpoints or product model names the abstract lists (for example particular sizes and variants of released models). Score the listing practice only.

channels.name: Enumerated list formatting inside the abstract
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract is organised as an explicit enumerated list — numbered or parenthesised items, 'First/Second/Finally' scaffolding, bulleted contributions. Score the formatting only, regardless of what the items say.

channels.name: Inline author-year citations inside the abstract
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how much the abstract cites prior work inline in author-year form (for example 'Smith et al., 2019') rather than referring to prior work in prose without citations. Score the citation practice only, not whether the citations are apt.

channels.name: Hedging-word density
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how heavily the abstract hedges — 'may', 'might', 'could', 'suggests', 'potential', 'appears to', 'we believe'. Count the hedging register only, not whether the hedging is warranted.

channels.name: Acronym density
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many distinct capitalised abbreviations the abstract introduces or uses per unit of text, counting field-standard acronyms as well as newly coined ones. Score density only.

channels.name: Rhetorical questions posed in the abstract
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract uses questions as a rhetorical device to frame its contribution ('Can a machine ...?', 'How can we ...?', 'This raises the question: ...'). Score the device only.

channels.name: Explicit count-signalling of experimental scale
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract advertises the COUNT of its experiments — 'extensive experiments on six benchmarks', 'four datasets', 'across three tasks', 'comprehensive evaluations'. Score the advertising of counts only, not the actual breadth of the evaluation.

channels.name: Scare-quoted or coined terms in quotation marks
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract puts terms in quotation marks to coin, hedge, or distance itself from them — 'false negatives', 'tabula rasa', 'middle way'. Score the quotation habit only.

channels.name: Famous benchmark and dataset name-dropping
channels.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many widely recognised benchmark or dataset names the abstract mentions (for example ImageNet, CIFAR, COCO, SuperGLUE, WMT, MNIST, LibriSpeech, Atari). Count recognisable names only; do not judge whether the evaluation is appropriate.

rep1.name: Membership in the learning-theory / optimization subfield
Mathematical notation density in the abstract
Enumeration of specific named models in a model zoo

rep2.name: A public repository URL appears in the abstract
Belief-change — the output is a changed understanding rather than a delivered artifact
Magnitude of the engineering or data resource the work required
Scare-quoted or coined terms in quotation marks

rep3.name: Poses a specific question and states its answer plainly
